source.title: Simply B1 Preliminary for Schools: 8 Complete Practice Tests (2019, revised exam from 2020)
source.answerKeyOrigin: Prepared for WordHop from the supplied reading text; not a publisher-provided answer key.
source.explanationOrigin: Written for WordHop with evidence from the supplied text.

questions.explanation: Adam asks George to send a message if he will be late, so the group knows whether to wait. He does not ask which bus George is on.
questions.evidence: Text us if you are going to be late and we'll wait and get a later bus.

questions.explanation: Sally says they have walked around Rome seeing its famous places. This describes sightseeing, rather than being tired of the walking.
questions.evidence: We have walked for hours every day — seeing all the famous places.

questions.explanation: Tina wants John to look at the hotel's website and say whether she should book it. Tina, rather than John, offers to make the booking.
questions.evidence: Have a look at the website I sent you and confirm if you want me to book it or not.

questions.explanation: The library closes at 2 pm on Friday and does not reopen until Monday. It is therefore closed over the weekend.
questions.evidence: It will be open from 9am to 2pm and then reopening, as usual, on Monday.

questions.explanation: Every entry must follow the animal theme. Owning a pet is not a requirement, and the two age groups are separate.
questions.evidence: The annual art competition this year is based on the theme of animals.

questions.explanation: Young World covers nature, environmental issues and ways to protect the environment. These interests match Tony's concern for animals and the natural world.
questions.evidence: Young World is a magazine for teenagers who care about their environment.

questions.explanation: Twist focuses on celebrities' fashion and helps readers develop their own style. This suits Gemma's interest in clothes design without making celebrity gossip the focus.
questions.evidence: Twist keeps you up-to-date on all of the fashion and beauty choices of our favourite celebs.

questions.explanation: Live your Life gives advice on health and personal problems, including confidence. It addresses both Martin's wish to get fitter and his difficulty settling into a new school.
questions.evidence: teenage health and problems

questions.explanation: J-14 reports on current young celebrities, including pop stars. Nick and Tony want to keep up with these stars' lives and activities.
questions.evidence: what Selena Gomez, One Direction, and other young stars are doing

questions.explanation: Teen Ink publishes writing by teenagers and includes fiction and poetry. Georgia can therefore read creative work written by people her own age.
questions.evidence: articles written only by teens and for teens

questions.explanation: Simon calls the hostel basic but warm and cosy. This means the accommodation was simple yet welcoming, rather than luxurious or unpleasant.
questions.evidence: It was a basic building but warm and cosy.

questions.explanation: Simon thinks tourists do not realise the problems they cause and need clear advice on behaving around ponies. He does not propose banning all tourists.
questions.evidence: there should be lots of notices everywhere, telling them how to behave near the ponies

questions.explanation: The passage identifies traffic as a danger to the ponies because tourists drive too quickly on roads through the forest.
questions.evidence: Unfortunately, many ponies are hit by cars every year.

questions.explanation: The experience changes Simon's study plans: he now wants a university degree related to animals. He still likes city life and intends to return to help.
questions.evidence: it has taught me that I want to study for a degree in animal behaviour

questions.explanation: The whole account describes helping the ponies, learning about the dangers they face and wanting to work with animals. Option A reflects this overall message.
questions.evidence: We were helping a charity that protects and counts the ponies that live in The New Forest.

questions.explanation: The previous sentence says young people had nothing to do. D gives the consequence: boredom and difficulty making friends, explaining why a club was needed.
questions.evidence: there was absolutely nothing for the young people to do after school and at the weekends

questions.explanation: The gap follows the offer of an empty shop. G explains why the owner allowed permanent use, and the next sentence adds that no payment was required.
questions.evidence: someone said we could have an old shop that had been closed for a year

questions.explanation: The previous sentence mentions putting furniture into the building. A explains that this furniture was donated, before the text lists other donated equipment.
questions.evidence: lots of people came to help us paint the rather dirty rooms and put furniture in it

questions.explanation: The following words 'There' and 'the cafe' need a place to refer to. H introduces the cafe where young people can buy drinks and snacks.
questions.evidence: There we can buy drinks and snacks. My mother often bakes cakes for the cafe.

questions.explanation: The previous sentence introduces the writer's little sister. C explains the noise she makes, which connects directly to the difficulty concentrating in the next sentence.
questions.evidence: I have to share a room with my little sister at home.

questions.explanation: The expression 'away from the crowds' means away from large groups of people. This fits the description of exclusive, less-visited parks.
questions.evidence: special holidays away from the (21) ...

questions.explanation: Adding Zanzibar helps create, or produce, the complete holiday experience. The other verbs do not express making an experience in this sentence.
questions.evidence: Then, add Zanzibar island to (22) ... the perfect beach and wildlife experience.

questions.explanation: 'Located in' describes where the parks are situated. 'Invented' and the other choices do not describe their geographical position appropriately.
questions.evidence: in the southern part of Tanzania

questions.explanation: The phrase 'compared with' is used to contrast the safari experience in the south with the experience in the north.
questions.evidence: a unique safari experience (24) ... with the northern part of the country

questions.explanation: A tourist destination is a place people travel to on holiday. Here the writer describes the northern part of Tanzania as the more usual place tourists visit.
questions.evidence: the more usual tourist (25) ...

questions.explanation: 'Exploring' means visiting and looking around places. It naturally describes what travellers can do on the beaches after their safari.
questions.evidence: find yourself (26) ... some of the best beaches in the world

questions.explanation: Use 'since' with the present perfect to introduce the point in time when an ongoing situation began: being twelve years old.
questions.evidence: I've had an American pen friend (27) ... I was twelve years old.

questions.explanation: 'Each other' is the reciprocal expression: both pen friends write letters to the other person.
questions.evidence: we have been writing to (28) ... other for four years

questions.explanation: A relative pronoun is needed to refer to a person, 'someone'. Both 'who' and 'that' can introduce this defining relative clause.
questions.evidence: someone (29) ... is the same age as you

questions.explanation: 'If' introduces the condition for the advice: a learner who wants better language skills should choose a pen friend who speaks that language. 'When' also fits this context.
questions.evidence: you should remember that (30) ... you want to improve your language skills

questions.explanation: 'Is' completes the clause describing what the pen friend's life is really like. 'Works' also gives a grammatical description of the way that life functions.
questions.evidence: see how their life really (31) ...

questions.explanation: 'People of all ages' means this activity is suitable for every age group, which supports the point that pen friends are not only for young people.
questions.evidence: you shouldn't think that pen friends are just for young people
